text:
Maya Chen: quick sync — results from the quant bakeoff are in, posted CSV to the gdrive link :point_right: https://redwood/gdrive/quant-bakeoff/mar24.csv
Jamal Singh: saw it, skimmed. AWQ-INT8 has ~2.6x throughput, 3.8ms median latency on p4d, but EM drop of 0.9 on QA set :thinking_face:
Olivia Park: GPTQ-INT8 is less aggressive: 1.9x throughput, 2.5ms median, EM drop 0.2 — seems like the best accuracy/perf tradeoff so far
Kai Morales: FP8 experiments were noisy — one seed shows small perf gain, another has catastrophic tokens with longer contexts. not safe for hosted yet :warning:
Maya Chen: agree. propose rollout plan: hosted: canary GPTQ-INT8 @ 5% with quality guardrails; Dedicated: staged 20% -> 50% based on latency/quality; Private: opt-in only for now
Jamal Singh: what are the guardrails exactly? need deterministic triggers for rollback and fallback
Olivia Park: EvalRunnerBot ran the nightly evals — latest numbers:
```
EvalRunnerBot: QA_EM: fp16=78.6, gptq-int8=78.4, awq-int8=77.7, fp8=76.9
EvalRunnerBot: RougeL_diff: gptq-int8 -0.3, awq-int8 -1.1
EvalRunnerBot: P95_latency (tokens/sec equiv) fp16=18.2ms, gptq-int8=9.6ms, awq-int8=7.9ms
```
Maya Chen: So GPTQ-INT8 delta is within our delta-SLO for hosted canary (<=0.5 EM), AWQ exceeds it. fallback should go to fp16/gptq-variant?
Kai Morales: fallback priority: 1) pinned fp16, 2) gptq-int8 (older stable build), 3) route to dedicated pool. Also add automatic rollback on eval-regression >0.7 EM for 10m window
Jamal Singh: suggest also adding runtime signal: if downstream perplexity jumps +5% or error_rate >0.5% or p95 latency > 3x baseline -> immediate fallback
Olivia Park: here's a proposed rollout policy block for the console (pseudoconfig):
```
rollout_policy: {
  strategy: "canary",
  canary_percent: 5,
  guardrails: {
    eval_delta_em_threshold: 0.5,
    eval_window_minutes: 15,
    runtime_error_rate_threshold: 0.5,
    runtime_perplexity_pct_increase: 5,
    latency_multiplier_threshold: 3
  },
  fallback_order: ["fp16","gptq-int8-stable","dedicated-fallback-pool"]
}
```
Maya Chen: love it. Ops: can we get deploy-bot to enforce the guardrails during canary and emit metrics to observability?
deploy-bot: canary started for model: redwood/llama2x-13b@gptq-int8, target=5% traffic, initiated by Maya Chen
Kai Morales: I'll wire up alerting to the canary channel and create a temporary dashboard for the next 2 days.
Jamal Singh: one more ask — add post-commit deterministic evals (subset of our regression suite) running every 5m during canary; if any test falls >0.4 EM -> auto-scale down and route to fp16
Olivia Park: we should record per-route token-cost delta too. If cost saving <15% it's not worth the risk for hosted customers with strict quality needs
Maya Chen: timeline: start canary tomorrow 09:00 PST, monitor for 24h, then expand to Dedicated 20% after 24h if stable. Private customers will get a changelog and opt-in instructions
Kai Morales: cc @sre-team and @security for FYI on fallback routing and key access
Jamal Singh: I'll draft the rollout playbook (steps, who runs manual rollback, escalation) and drop in the runbook folder
Olivia Park: nice — I'll update the model card with quantization notes and accuracy deltas
Maya Chen: thanks everyone. tagging this thread as the source of truth for the rollout. Please post any post-canary anomalies here :eyes:
deploy-bot: canary metrics: 5% traffic live, p95_latency=10.1ms, error_rate=0.03%, eval_runner_last=OK
Maya Chen: perfect — will kick off the canary tomorrow.
